axes.label: Craft & polish
axes.description: Visual quality, typography, colour, composition, motion feel, finish. Would a discerning person believe a human designed this on purpose?

axes.label: Technical ambition
axes.description: How hard is what was actually built, and is it built correctly? Real technique versus the cheapest thing that looks similar.

axes.label: Brief adherence
axes.description: Did it do everything the prompt asked, completely, including the output contract? Stubs and TODOs count against.

axes.label: Originality
axes.description: Is the idea and its execution distinctive, or is it the median AI answer to this prompt?

redFlags: Dead GLSL in the thread fragment shader: two `draw` expressions are computed then immediately overwritten by a third.
`fogNight.clone().lerp(...)` allocates a Color object every frame, directly contrary to the stated no-per-frame-allocation requirement.
Finale typography is effectively unreadable in the settled end state (blown-out sun plus ~10% text opacity at p=1).
A new fog Color is allocated every rendered frame via `fogNight.clone().lerp(fogDawn, warm)` instead of reusing a color object. This is small but unnecessary per-frame garbage.
The thread fragment shader contains two earlier `draw` calculations that are immediately overwritten by a third assignment, indicating dead shader logic rather than a clean finalized implementation.

No teardown/disposal path exists for renderer, geometries, materials, or event listeners if this page were mounted and unmounted; less consequential for a standalone document, but it falls short of the stated disposal/reuse ideal.
Uncaught SyntaxError ('Invalid or unexpected token') from an unterminated string literal in tryBoost() — the whole script fails to execute.
Measured 0 fps and 0.04 mean pixel delta under keyboard input: the WebGL canvas is never created, so the game loop, collision, scoring and audio are all dead code in practice.
Output contract breach: the document logs a console error and does not run correctly when opened directly.

Fatal syntax error in `tryBoost()`: `elFlash.style.background='#9ff;` has an unterminated string literal. This matches the automated `Invalid or unexpected token` console error and explains the measured 0 FPS and negligible keyboard pixel delta.
All game mechanics are unreachable because a JavaScript parse error prevents the entire script from executing, not merely the boost feature.
Console error: Invalid or unexpected token (broken JS string literal).
Game loop never starts; 0 fps and no meaningful interaction.
Violates “must not throw uncaught errors” / finished playable deliverable.
External Google Fonts are requested, which undermines strict offline operation even though CDN usage is separately permitted.

The footer says “No network calls,” but the document loads three Google Fonts resources via fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com. Those CDN requests are allowed by the output contract, but the marketing claim is factually inaccurate.

The bespoke closing SVG appears to render an unexplained “PV” mark rather than a recognizably relevant Grok/xAI mark. It reads like an accidental or unmotivated artifact in an otherwise carefully authored identity treatment.

Automated browser evidence reports one uncaught syntax error: “Invalid or unexpected token.”

Geometry exceeds the viewBox and is clipped: the buoy waterline ends at x=25.2 and the tide-gauge waterline at x=26.0 in a 0 0 24 24 box, contradicting the stated 'nothing clipped' requirement.

`@supports (anchor-name: --x) { .more a { anchor-name: --open } }` declares an anchor name that nothing positions against — a spec name ticked off with no effect.

Automated capture reports a console error from the Google Fonts request (`net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB`). This appears environment/CDN related rather than a JavaScript error, but it means the delivered font loading was not clean in the measured run.

The reading-position rail/progress treatment depends on scroll-driven animation support; the stated fallback is deliberate, but unsupported browsers have no persistent section indicator and a permanently empty progress line.
